questions.text:
If ‘\(\rightarrow\)’ denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words [walk \(\rightarrow\) jog \(\rightarrow\) sprint] is analogous to [bothered \(\rightarrow\) ________ \(\rightarrow\) daunted].

Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.solution: Walk, jog and sprint are the same action at rising intensity. Bothered, fazed and daunted are the same feeling (being disturbed) at rising intensity: fazed means disconcerted, stronger than bothered and weaker than daunted. Phased, phrased and fused are unrelated words that only sound similar.

questions.text:
Two wizards try to create a spell using all the four elements, water, air, fire, and earth. For this, they decide to mix all these elements in all possible orders. They also decide to work independently. After trying all possible combination of elements, they conclude that the spell does not work.

How many attempts does each wizard make before coming to this conclusion, independently?
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.solution: Each wizard works alone and tries every order of the four elements: \(4! = 24\) attempts. Working independently means the attempts are not shared, so each makes 24.

questions.text:
In an engineering college of 10,000 students, 1,500 like neither their core branches nor other branches. The number of students who like their core branches is 1/4th of the number of students who like other branches. The number of students who like both their core and other branches is 500.

The number of students who like their core branches is
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.solution:
Students who like at least one: \(10000 - 1500 = 8500\).
Let \(C\) like core and \(O\) like other branches, with \(C = O/4\). Then \(C + O - 500 = 8500\), so \(C + O = 9000\).
\(C + 4C = 9000 \Rightarrow C = 1800\).

questions.text:
For positive non-zero real variables \(x\) and \(y\), if
\[\ln\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\left[\ln(x) + \ln(y)\right]\]
then, the value of \(\frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{x}\) is
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.solution:
The right side is \(\ln\sqrt{xy}\), so \(\frac{x+y}{2} = \sqrt{xy}\).
Then \((\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y})^2 = 0\), so \(x = y\).
Hence \(\frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{x} = 1 + 1 = 2\).

questions.text: In the sequence 6, 9, 14, \(x\), 30, 41, a possible value of \(x\) is
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.solution:
Differences: \(9 - 6 = 3\), \(14 - 9 = 5\), \(41 - 30 = 11\). The differences are consecutive odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9, 11.
So \(x = 14 + 7 = 21\), and \(21 + 9 = 30\) checks.

questions.text:
Sequence the following sentences in a coherent passage.

P: This fortuitous geological event generated a colossal amount of energy and heat that resulted in the rocks rising to an average height of 4 km across the contact zone.

Q: Thus, the geophysicists tend to think of the Himalayas as an active geological event rather than as a static geological feature.

R: The natural process of the cooling of this massive edifice absorbed large quantities of atmospheric carbon dioxide, altering the earth’s atmosphere and making it better suited for life.

S: Many millennia ago, a breakaway chunk of bedrock from the Antarctic Plate collided with the massive Eurasian Plate.
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.solution: S opens the story (the collision). P follows: "this fortuitous geological event" is the collision, and it raised the rocks. R refers to "this massive edifice", the raised rock mass, and its cooling. Q begins with "Thus" and draws the conclusion. Order: SPRQ.

questions.text: A person sold two different items at the same price. He made 10% profit in one item, and 10% loss in the other item. In selling these two items, the person made a total of
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.solution:
Let each selling price be 99. Cost of the first item: \(99/1.1 = 90\). Cost of the second: \(99/0.9 = 110\).
Total cost 200, total selling price 198: a loss of 2 on 200, that is 1%.
In general, equal selling prices with \(x\%\) profit and \(x\%\) loss give a loss of \(x^2/100\) per cent, here 1%.

questions.text:
The pie charts depict the shares of various power generation technologies in the total electricity generation of a country for the years 2007 and 2023.

| Technology | Year 2007 | Year 2023 |
|---|---|---|
| Coal | 35% | 20% |
| Gas | 25% | 15% |
| Wind | 5% | 10% |
| Hydro | 30% | 35% |
| Solar | 5% | 20% |

The renewable sources of electricity generation consist of Hydro, Solar and Wind. Assuming that the total electricity generated remains the same from 2007 to 2023, what is the percentage increase in the share of the renewable sources of electricity generation over this period?
questions.subject: General Aptitude

questions.text:
A cube is to be cut into 8 pieces of equal size and shape. Here, each cut should be straight and it should not stop till it reaches the other end of the cube.

The minimum number of such cuts required is
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.solution: One cut through the middle parallel to each pair of opposite faces: three mutually perpendicular cuts split the cube into \(2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8\) equal smaller cubes. Two straight cuts give at most 4 pieces, so 3 is the minimum.

questions.text:
In the 4 \(\times\) 4 array shown below, each cell of the first three rows has either a cross (X) or a number.

The number in a cell represents the count of the immediate neighboring cells (left, right, top, bottom, diagonals) NOT having a cross (X). Given that the last row has no crosses (X), the sum of the four numbers to be filled in the last row is

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | X | 4 | 3 |
| X | 5 | 5 | 4 |
| 3 | X | 6 | X |
| | | | |
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.solution:
Row 3 reads 3, X, 6, X and row 4 has no crosses.
Cell 1 of row 4: neighbours (3,1), (3,2) = X, (4,2). Non-cross count 2.
Cell 2: neighbours (3,1), (3,2) = X, (3,3), (4,1), (4,3). Count 4.
Cell 3: neighbours (3,2) = X, (3,3), (3,4) = X, (4,2), (4,4). Count 3.
Cell 4: neighbours (3,3), (3,4) = X, (4,3). Count 2.
Sum \(= 2 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 11\).

questions.text: Consider a computer with a 4 MHz processor. Its DMA controller can transfer 8 bytes in 1 cycle from a device to main memory through cycle stealing at regular intervals. Which one of the following is the data transfer rate (in bits per second) of the DMA controller if 1% of the processor cycles are used for DMA?
questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.solution:
Cycles per second: \(4 \times 10^6\). DMA uses 1%: \(4 \times 10^4\) cycles per second.
Each cycle moves 8 bytes = 64 bits.
Rate \(= 4 \times 10^4 \times 64 = 2{,}560{,}000\) bits per second, written 25,60,000.

questions.text:
Let \(p\) and \(q\) be the following propositions:

\(p\): Fail grade can be given.

\(q\): Student scores more than 50% marks.

Consider the statement: “Fail grade cannot be given when student scores more than 50% marks.”

Which one of the following is the CORRECT representation of the above statement in propositional logic?
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution: "A when B" means "if B then A". Here B is \(q\) (scores more than 50%) and A is "fail grade cannot be given", \(\neg p\). So the statement is \(q \rightarrow \neg p\).

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
Arguments of f are evaluated right to left: h(20) prints 20, then g(10) prints 10. So f is called with x = 10, y = 20.
Inside f: g(x) prints 10, then h(y) prints 20.
Output: 20101020.

questions.text:
The format of a single-precision floating-point number as per the IEEE 754 standard is:

| Sign (1bit) | Exponent (8 bits) | Mantissa (23 bits) |
|---|---|---|

Choose the largest floating-point number among the following options.
questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.solution:
A: exponent 127, value \(1.11\ldots1_2 \times 2^{0}\), just under 2.
B: exponent 254, the largest normal exponent, value \((2 - 2^{-23}) \times 2^{127}\): the largest finite single-precision number.
C: exponent all ones with a non-zero mantissa is NaN, not a number at all.
D: exponent 127, mantissa zero: value 1.
The largest number is B.

questions.text:
Let \(T(n)\) be the recurrence relation defined as follows:

\(T(0) = 1\),
\(T(1) = 2\), and
\(T(n) = 5T(n-1) - 6T(n-2)\) for \(n \geq 2\)

Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.solution:
Characteristic equation \(r^2 - 5r + 6 = 0\), roots 2 and 3, so \(T(n) = a2^n + b3^n\).
\(T(0) = a + b = 1\), \(T(1) = 2a + 3b = 2\). Subtracting twice the first: \(b = 0\), \(a = 1\).
So \(T(n) = 2^n\) exactly, which is \(\Theta(2^n)\).

questions.text:
Let \(f(x)\) be a continuous function from \(\mathbb{R}\) to \(\mathbb{R}\) such that
\[f(x) = 1 - f(2 - x)\]
Which one of the following options is the CORRECT value of \(\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\,dx\) ?
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let \(I = \int_0^2 f(x)\,dx\). Substituting \(x \to 2 - x\) gives \(\int_0^2 f(2-x)\,dx = I\) as well.
Integrate the given relation over \([0, 2]\): \(I = \int_0^2 1\,dx - \int_0^2 f(2-x)\,dx = 2 - I\).
So \(2I = 2\) and \(I = 1\).

questions.text: Let \(A\) be the adjacency matrix of a simple undirected graph \(G\). Suppose \(A\) is its own inverse. Which one of the following statements is always TRUE?
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
\(A\) is its own inverse means \(A^2 = I\).
The diagonal entry \((A^2)_{ii}\) is the degree of vertex \(i\), so every vertex has degree exactly 1.
The off-diagonal entry \((A^2)_{ij}\) counts common neighbours, and these are 0, which degree 1 already ensures.
A graph in which every vertex has degree exactly 1 is a perfect matching. Such graphs exist (for example a single edge), so D is wrong; a cycle and a complete graph on 3 or more vertices have degree at least 2.

questions.text: When six unbiased dice are rolled simultaneously, the probability of getting all distinct numbers (i.e., 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6) is
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
Total outcomes: \(6^6 = 46656\). Favourable: the six dice show 1 to 6 in some order, \(6! = 720\).
Probability \(= \frac{720}{46656} = \frac{5}{324}\).

questions.text: Once the DBMS informs the user that a transaction has been successfully completed, its effect should persist even if the system crashes before all its changes are reflected on disk. This property is called
questions.subject: Databases
questions.solution: Durability is the guarantee that the effects of a committed transaction survive later failures, including a crash before the changes reach disk (the log is used to redo them). Atomicity is all or nothing, consistency is preserving integrity constraints, isolation is non-interference of concurrent transactions.

questions.text: In the context of owner and weak entity sets in the ER (Entity-Relationship) data model, which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.label: A
options.text: The weak entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship

options.label: B
options.text: The owner entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship

options.label: C
options.text: Both weak and owner entity sets MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship

options.label: D
options.text: Neither weak entity set nor owner entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship

questions.subject: Databases
questions.solution: A weak entity cannot be identified without its owner, so every weak entity must take part in the identifying relationship: total participation on the weak side. An owner entity may have no weak entities attached, so its participation can be partial.

questions.text:
Consider the following two sets:

| Set X | Set Y |
|---|---|
| P. Lexical Analyzer | 1. Abstract Syntax Tree |
| Q. Syntax Analyzer | 2. Token |
| R. Intermediate Code Generator | 3. Parse Tree |
| S. Code Optimizer | 4. Constant Folding |

Which one of the following options is the CORRECT match from Set X to Set Y ?
questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.solution: The lexical analyzer produces tokens (P, 2). The syntax analyzer builds the parse tree (Q, 3). The intermediate code generator works with the abstract syntax tree, a common intermediate representation (R, 1). Constant folding is a code optimisation (S, 4). Match: P 2, Q 3, R 1, S 4.

questions.text: Which one of the following regular expressions is equivalent to the language accepted by the DFA given below?
questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.solution:
The DFA has a start state with a 0 self-loop, a 1 edge to the accepting state, a 0 self-loop on the accepting state and a 1 edge back. It accepts exactly the strings with an odd number of 1s.
A: \(0^*1\) reaches the accepting state; then each \(0\) stays and each \(10^*1\) leaves and returns. This generates every string with an odd number of 1s. Correct.
B: contains \(\epsilon\) (no 1s). Wrong.
C: cannot generate 111, which has three 1s: after the first 1, every starred block begins with 0. Wrong.
D: every string must begin with 0, so "1" is missed. Wrong.

questions.text:
Node X has a TCP connection open to node Y. The packets from X to Y go through an intermediate IP router R. Ethernet switch S is the first switch on the network path between X and R. Consider a packet sent from X to Y over this connection.

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the destination IP and MAC addresses on this packet at the time it leaves X?

options.label: A
options.text: The destination IP address is the IP address of R

options.label: B
options.text: The destination IP address is the IP address of Y

options.label: C
options.text: The destination MAC address is the MAC address of S

options.label: D
options.text: The destination MAC address is the MAC address of Y

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.chapter: IP Addressing, Fragmentation and Support Protocols
questions.solution:
A: wrong. The IP header carries the end-to-end destination, which is Y, not the router.
B: correct, for the same reason.
C: wrong. An Ethernet switch is transparent at layer 2; frames are never addressed to it.
D: wrong. Y is on another network (beyond router R), so the frame is addressed to the next hop, R's MAC address.

questions.text: Which of the following tasks is/are the responsibility/responsibilities of the memory management unit (MMU) in a system with paging-based memory management?

options.label: A
options.text: Allocate a new page table for a newly created process

options.label: B
options.text: Translate a virtual address to a physical address using the page table

options.label: C
options.text: Raise a trap when a virtual address is not found in the page table

options.label: D
options.text: Raise a trap when a process tries to write to a page marked with read-only permission in the page table

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.solution:
A: wrong. Allocating and filling a page table is the operating system's job, done in software when a process is created.
B: correct. Address translation through the page table (and TLB) is the MMU's core hardware task.
C: correct. When a mapping is missing or invalid, the MMU raises a page fault trap for the OS to handle.
D: correct. The MMU checks the protection bits on each access and traps on a write to a read-only page.

questions.text: Consider a process P running on a CPU. Which one or more of the following events will always trigger a context switch by the OS that results in process P moving to a non-running state (e.g., ready, blocked)?

options.label: A
options.text: P makes a blocking system call to read a block of data from the disk

options.label: B
options.text: P tries to access a page that is in the swap space, triggering a page fault

options.label: C
options.text: An interrupt is raised by the disk to deliver data requested by some other process

options.label: D
options.text: A timer interrupt is raised by the hardware

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.solution:
A: correct. A blocking disk read cannot complete at once, so P is moved to the blocked state and another process is scheduled.
B: correct. The page must be brought in from the swap space on disk, so P blocks until that I/O completes.
C: wrong. The interrupt is serviced and the other process is made ready, but P may simply resume; a switch is not guaranteed.
D: wrong. A timer interrupt does not always end P's time slice (the quantum may not have expired), so P need not leave the running state.

questions.text: Which of the following file organizations is/are I/O efficient for the scan operation in DBMS?
questions.subject: Databases
questions.solution:
A scan reads every record.
A and B: correct. A sorted file and a heap file are read page by page, about \(B\) I/Os for \(B\) data pages, which is optimal.
C and D: wrong. Scanning through an unclustered index visits records in index order, which can mean one page I/O per record (about \(B \times R\) I/Os for \(R\) records per page), far worse than reading the file directly.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the Two Phase Locking (2PL) protocol is/are TRUE?

options.label: B
options.text: With 2PL, a transaction always locks the data item being read or written just before every operation and always releases the lock just after the operation

options.label: C
options.text: With 2PL, once a lock is released on any data item inside a transaction, no more locks on any data item can be obtained inside that transaction

questions.subject: Databases
questions.solution:
A: correct. Every schedule allowed by 2PL is conflict serializable (order transactions by their lock points).
B: wrong. Releasing each lock right after its operation and locking again later breaks the growing and shrinking phases; 2PL forbids it.
C: correct. This is the definition: after the first unlock (shrinking phase starts), no new lock may be acquired.
D: correct. T1 holds a lock on X and waits for Y while T2 holds Y and waits for X: 2PL does not prevent this deadlock.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about IPv4 fragmentation is/are TRUE?

options.label: A
options.text: The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed only at the source of the datagram

options.label: B
options.text: The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed at any IP router which finds that the size of the datagram to be transmitted exceeds the MTU

options.label: C
options.text: The reassembly of fragments is performed only at the destination of the datagram

options.label: D
options.text: The reassembly of fragments is performed at all intermediate routers along the path from the source to the destination

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.chapter: IP Addressing, Fragmentation and Support Protocols
questions.solution:
A: wrong. In IPv4 any router may fragment (unless DF is set); only IPv6 restricts fragmentation to the source.
B: correct. A router whose outgoing link MTU is smaller than the datagram fragments it.
C: correct. Fragments may take different paths, so only the final destination reassembles them.
D: wrong. Intermediate routers do not reassemble.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are FALSE?

options.label: A
options.text: An attribute grammar is a syntax-directed definition (SDD) in which the functions in the semantic rules have no side effects

options.label: B
options.text: The attributes in a L-attributed definition cannot always be evaluated in a depth-first order

options.label: C
options.text: Synthesized attributes can be evaluated by a bottom-up parser as the input is parsed

options.label: D
options.text: All L-attributed definitions based on LR(1) grammar can be evaluated using a bottom-up parsing strategy

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.solution:
A: true. An SDD whose semantic rules have no side effects is what is called an attribute grammar.
B: false. In an L-attributed definition every inherited attribute depends only on the parent and on siblings to its left, so a left-to-right depth-first traversal can always evaluate all attributes. The statement says the opposite.
C: true. Synthesized attributes are computed when a production is reduced, so an LR parser evaluates them while parsing (S-attributed definitions).
D: false. Bottom-up evaluation of L-attributed definitions (with marker non-terminals) is guaranteed for those based on LL(1) grammars; inserting markers into an arbitrary LR(1) grammar can create conflicts, so not all can be done bottom-up.
The FALSE statements are B and D.

questions.text: For a Boolean variable \(x\), which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.solution:
A: true (identity law).
B: false. \(x + 1 = 1\), which differs from \(x\) when \(x = 0\).
C: false. \(x.x = x\) (idempotence), which is 1 when \(x = 1\).
D: true (complement law).

questions.text:
An instruction format has the following structure:

Instruction Number: Opcode destination reg, source reg-1, source reg-2

Consider the following sequence of instructions to be executed in a pipelined processor:

```text
I1: DIV R3, R1, R2
I2: SUB R5, R3, R4
I3: ADD R3, R5, R6
I4: MUL R7, R3, R8
```

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

options.label: A
options.text: There is a RAW dependency on R3 between I1 and I2

options.label: B
options.text: There is a WAR dependency on R3 between I1 and I3

options.label: C
options.text: There is a RAW dependency on R3 between I2 and I3

options.label: D
options.text: There is a WAW dependency on R3 between I3 and I4

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.solution:
I1 writes R3; I2 reads R3; I3 writes R3; I4 reads R3.
A: true. I2 reads R3 after I1 writes it: read after write.
B: false. I1 and I3 both write R3: that is WAW, not WAR.
C: false. I2 reads R3 and the later I3 writes it: that is WAR, not RAW.
D: false. I3 writes R3 and I4 reads it: that is RAW, not WAW.

questions.text: Which of the following fields of an IP header is/are always modified by any router before it forwards the IP packet?
questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.chapter: IP Addressing, Fragmentation and Support Protocols
questions.solution:
A: wrong. The source address is end-to-end; an ordinary router leaves it alone (only NAT changes it, and not every router does NAT).
B: wrong. The protocol field names the payload (TCP, UDP) and does not change.
C: correct. Every router decrements TTL.
D: correct. Since TTL changes, the header checksum must be recomputed at every hop.

options.label: A
options.text: The function call fX("abcd") will always return a value

options.label: B
options.text: Assuming a character array c is declared as char c[] = "abcd" in main(), the function call fX(c)will always return a value

options.label: C
options.text: The code of the function will not compile

options.label: D
options.text: Assuming a character pointer c is declared as char *c = "abcd" in main(), the function call fX(c)will always return a value

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
fX walks b to the terminating '\0' and returns the pointer difference, the string length.
A: true. A string literal is null-terminated, so the loop stops and 4 is returned.
B: true. char c[] = "abcd" makes a 5-byte array including '\0'; fX(c) returns 4.
C: false. The code is valid C; subtracting two char pointers gives an integer.
D: true. c points to the null-terminated literal "abcd"; fX(c) returns 4.

questions.text:
Let \(P\) be the partial order defined on the set \(\{1,2,3,4\}\) as follows
\[P = \{(x, x) \mid x \in \{1,2,3,4\}\} \cup \{(1,2), (3,2), (3,4)\}\]
The number of total orders on \(\{1,2,3,4\}\) that contain \(P\) is __________
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
A total order containing \(P\) must place 1 before 2, 3 before 2 and 3 before 4.
The first element must be minimal: 1 or 3.
First 1: the rest is \(\{2,3,4\}\) with 3 before 2 and 3 before 4, so 3 comes next and 2, 4 follow in either order: 2 orders.
First 3: the rest is \(\{1,2,4\}\) with only 1 before 2: \(3!/2 = 3\) orders.
Total \(= 2 + 3 = 5\).

questions.text: Let \(A\) be an array containing integer values. The distance of \(A\) is defined as the minimum number of elements in \(A\) that must be replaced with another integer so that the resulting array is sorted in non-decreasing order. The distance of the array [2, 5, 3, 1, 4, 2, 6] is ___________
questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.solution:
The elements kept unchanged must already form a non-decreasing subsequence, so distance \(= n - \) (length of the longest non-decreasing subsequence).
Longest non-decreasing subsequence of [2, 5, 3, 1, 4, 2, 6]: 2, 3, 4, 6, length 4 (no length 5 exists: after 2, 3, 4 only 6 can follow, and 5 is followed by only 6).
Keep 2, 3, 4, 6 and replace 5 by 3, 1 by 4 and 2 by 5: [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6], sorted.
Distance \(= 7 - 4 = 3\).

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
q = p + 1 points to a[1]. Subtracting two pointers to the same array gives the number of elements between them, not bytes: q - p = 1.
*q - *p = 25.0 - 20.0 = 5.0, cast to int gives 5.
Output: 1,5.

questions.text:
Consider a single processor system with four processes A, B, C, and D, represented as given below, where for each process the first value is its arrival time, and the second value is its CPU burst time.

A (0, 10), B (2, 6), C (4, 3), and D (6, 7).

Which one of the following options gives the average waiting times when preemptive Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF) and Non-Preemptive Shortest Job First (NP-SJF) CPU scheduling algorithms are applied to the processes?
questions.subject: Operating System
questions.solution:
SRTF: A runs 0 to 2 (8 left). B arrives with 6 < 8, runs 2 to 4 (4 left). C arrives with 3 < 4, runs 4 to 7 (D arrives at 6 with 7, C keeps running). At 7: B 4, D 7, A 8, so B runs 7 to 11, D 11 to 18, A 18 to 26.
Waiting = finish \(-\) arrival \(-\) burst: A \(26 - 0 - 10 = 16\), B \(11 - 2 - 6 = 3\), C \(7 - 4 - 3 = 0\), D \(18 - 6 - 7 = 5\). Average \(24/4 = 6\).
NP-SJF: A runs 0 to 10. Then C (3) 10 to 13, B (6) 13 to 19, D (7) 19 to 26.
Waiting: A 0, C \(10 - 4 = 6\), B \(13 - 2 = 11\), D \(19 - 6 = 13\). Average \(30/4 = 7.5\).

questions.text: Which one of the following CIDR prefixes exactly represents the range of IP addresses 10.12.2.0 to 10.12.3.255?
questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.chapter: IP Addressing, Fragmentation and Support Protocols
questions.solution:
The range has \(2 \times 256 = 512 = 2^9\) addresses, so the prefix length is \(32 - 9 = 23\).
The third octet 2 is 00000010; with a /23 mask its last bit is host bits, and 2 is even, so 10.12.2.0 is a valid /23 block start covering 10.12.2.0 to 10.12.3.255.
/24 covers only 10.12.2.x; /22 blocks cover 1024 addresses (10.12.0.0 to 10.12.3.255).

questions.text:
You are given a set \(V\) of distinct integers. A binary search tree \(T\) is created by inserting all elements of \(V\) one by one, starting with an empty tree. The tree \(T\) follows the convention that, at each node, all values stored in the left subtree of the node are smaller than the value stored at the node. You are not aware of the sequence in which these values were inserted into \(T\), and you do not have access to \(T\).

Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.label: A
options.text: Inorder traversal of \(T\) can be determined from \(V\)

options.label: B
options.text: Root node of \(T\) can be determined from \(V\)

options.label: C
options.text: Preorder traversal of \(T\) can be determined from \(V\)

options.label: D
options.text: Postorder traversal of \(T\) can be determined from \(V\)

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.chapter: Trees, Binary Search Trees and Heaps
questions.solution:
The inorder traversal of any BST lists its keys in increasing order, so it is just \(V\) sorted, whatever the insertion order.
The root is the first value inserted, and the preorder and postorder traversals depend on the tree's shape, which depends on the unknown insertion order. Only A can be determined.

questions.text:
Consider the following context-free grammar where the start symbol is \(S\) and the set of terminals is \(\{a,b,c,d\}\).

\(S \rightarrow AaAb \mid BbBa\)
\(A \rightarrow cS \mid \epsilon\)
\(B \rightarrow dS \mid \epsilon\)

The following is a partially-filled LL(1) parsing table.

| | \(a\) | \(b\) | \(c\) | \(d\) | $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(S\) | \(S \rightarrow AaAb\) | \(S \rightarrow BbBa\) | (1) | (2) | |
| \(A\) | \(A \rightarrow \epsilon\) | (3) | \(A \rightarrow cS\) | | |
| \(B\) | (4) | \(B \rightarrow \epsilon\) | | \(B \rightarrow dS\) | |

Which one of the following options represents the CORRECT combination for the numbered cells in the parsing table?

Note: In the options, “blank” denotes that the corresponding cell is empty.
questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.solution:
FIRST(\(AaAb\)) \(= \{c, a\}\) (A is c or empty), so \(S \rightarrow AaAb\) goes under a and c: cell (1) is \(S \rightarrow AaAb\).
FIRST(\(BbBa\)) \(= \{d, b\}\), so \(S \rightarrow BbBa\) goes under b and d: cell (2) is \(S \rightarrow BbBa\).
FOLLOW(\(A\)): in \(AaAb\) the first A is followed by a and the second by b, so FOLLOW(\(A\)) \(= \{a, b\}\). \(A \rightarrow \epsilon\) goes under a and b: cell (3) is \(A \rightarrow \epsilon\).
FOLLOW(\(B\)) \(= \{b, a\}\) from \(BbBa\): cell (4) is \(B \rightarrow \epsilon\).

questions.text:
Let \(M\) be the 5-state NFA with \(\epsilon\)-transitions shown in the diagram below.

Which one of the following regular expressions represents the language accepted by \(M\) ?
questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.solution:
From start state 1, \(\epsilon\)-moves go to 2 (accepting) and 4.
Branch via 2: 2 and 3 swap on 0, so state 2 is reached by \((00)^*\) (accepted). State 3 is reached by \(0(00)^*\); its \(\epsilon\)-move goes to 5 (accepting), and 5 and 4 swap on 1, so 5 is revisited by \((11)^*\): \(0(00)^*(11)^*\).
Branch via 4: 4 goes to 5 on 1, then \((11)^*\): \(1(11)^*\).
Language: \((00)^* + 0(00)^*(11)^* + 1(11)^* = (00)^* + (1 + 0(00)^*)(11)^*\).
B: \(0^* = (00)^* + 0(00)^*\), and \(0(00)^*\) is already in the second term, so B equals the language.
A misses 0. C contains 11, which M rejects. D misses \(\epsilon\), which M accepts.

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.solution:
At the start of iteration i, first = X[i-1] and second is the other value in the current two-value window.
If X[i] equals second: X[i] differs from X[i-1], so a new run of equal values starts: len1 = 1, (P) = 1. The window still has two values, so len2 grows by 1.
If X[i] is a new value: the longest two-value subarray ending at X[i] is the run of X[i-1] values (length len1) plus X[i], so len2 = len1 + 1, (Q) = len1+1.
Option B.

questions.text:
Consider the following expression: \(x[i] = (p + r) * -s[i] + u/w\). The following sequence shows the list of triples representing the given expression, with entries missing for triples (1), (3), and (6).

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| (0) | + | \(p\) | \(r\) |
| (1) | | | |
| (2) | uminus | (1) | |
| (3) | | | |
| (4) | / | \(u\) | \(w\) |
| (5) | + | (3) | (4) |
| (6) | | | |
| (7) | = | (6) | (5) |

Which one of the following options fills in the missing entries CORRECTLY?
questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.solution:
(1) reads the array element s[i]: the indexed-load operator =[] with operands s and i.
(2) negates it, and (3) multiplies the sum (0) by (2): * (0) (2).
(6) forms the array location x[i] for storing: []= with operands x and i. Then (7) assigns (5) to that location: = (6) (5).
Option A. B and D use the wrong operators in (1) and (3); C gives (6) the operand (5), but the value is supplied by triple (7).

questions.text: Let \(x\) and \(y\) be random variables, not necessarily independent, that take real values in the interval \([0,1]\). Let \(z = xy\) and let the mean values of \(x, y, z\) be \(\bar{x}, \bar{y}, \bar{z}\), respectively. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since \(0 \leq y \leq 1\) and \(x \geq 0\), \(z = xy \leq x\) always, so \(\bar{z} \leq \bar{x}\): D is always true.
\(\bar{z} - \bar{x}\bar{y} = \mathrm{Cov}(x, y)\), which can be positive (take \(y = x\)) or negative (take \(y = 1 - x\)), so A, B and C each fail for some pair.

questions.text:
The relation schema, Person(pid,city), describes the city of residence for every person uniquely identified by pid. The following relational algebra operators are available: selection, projection, cross product, and rename.

To find the list of cities where at least 3 persons reside, using the above operators, the minimum number of cross product operations that must be used is
questions.subject: Databases
questions.chapter: Relational Algebra, Tuple Calculus and SQL
questions.solution:
Three different persons in the same city must appear together in one tuple, so three copies of Person (renamed P1, P2, P3) are needed: \(P1 	imes P2 	imes P3\), two cross products.
Then select P1.city = P2.city = P3.city with P1.pid \(
eq\) P2.pid, P1.pid \(
eq\) P3.pid, P2.pid \(
eq\) P3.pid, and project the city.
With only one cross product a tuple holds two persons, which can test "at least 2" but not "at least 3". Minimum: 2.

options.label: A
options.text: T1 runs first and prints 1, T2 runs next and prints 2

options.label: B
options.text: T2 runs first and prints 1, T1 runs next and prints 2

options.label: C
options.text: T1 runs first and prints 1, T2 does not print anything (deadlock)

options.label: D
options.text: T2 runs first and prints 1, T1 does not print anything (deadlock)

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.solution:
A: impossible. If T1 gets s1 first, it prints 1 and then waits on s2 (value 0) while still holding s1. T2 blocks on wait(s1), so it never prints.
B: possible. T2 gets s1, prints 1, signals s2 and s1. T1 then gets s1, prints 2, and wait(s2) succeeds.
C: possible. This is exactly the case in A: T1 prints 1 and both threads are stuck.
D: impossible. After T2 finishes it has released s1 and set s2 to 1, so T1 always completes and prints 2.

questions.text: Let \(A\) be an \(n \times n\) matrix over the set of all real numbers \(\mathbb{R}\). Let \(B\) be a matrix obtained from \(A\) by swapping two rows. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

options.label: A
options.text: The determinant of \(B\) is the negative of the determinant of \(A\)

options.label: B
options.text: If \(A\) is invertible, then \(B\) is also invertible

options.label: C
options.text: If \(A\) is symmetric, then \(B\) is also symmetric

options.label: D
options.text: If the trace of \(A\) is zero, then the trace of \(B\) is also zero

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
A: true. A row swap changes the sign of the determinant.
B: true. \(\det B = -\det A \neq 0\).
C: false. \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\ 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}\) is symmetric, but swapping rows gives \(\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3\\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\), which is not.
D: false. \(A = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\) has trace 0, but swapping rows gives \(\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0\\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\) with trace 1.

questions.text:
Let S1 and S2 be two stacks. S1 has capacity of 4 elements. S2 has capacity of 2 elements. S1 already has 4 elements: 100, 200, 300, and 400, whereas S2 is empty, as shown below.

| Stack S1 | Stack S2 |
|---|---|
| 400 (Top) | |
| 300 | |
| 200 | |
| 100 | |

Only the following three operations are available:

PushToS2: Pop the top element from S1 and push it on S2.

PushToS1: Pop the top element from S2 and push it on S1.

GenerateOutput: Pop the top element from S1 and output it to the user.

Note that the pop operation is not allowed on an empty stack and the push operation is not allowed on a full stack.

Which of the following output sequences can be generated by using the above operations?
questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.chapter: Arrays, Stacks, Queues and Linked Lists
questions.solution:
Only S1's top can be output, and S2 holds at most 2 elements.
A: impossible. To output 100 first, 400, 300 and 200 must all leave S1, but S2 holds only two.
B: possible. Move 400, 300 to S2; output 200; move 300 back and output it; move 400 back and output it; output 100.
C: possible. Output 400; move 300 to S2; output 200, output 100; move 300 back and output it.
D: possible. Move 400 to S2; output 300, output 200; move 400 back and output it; output 100.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are EQUAL to 224 in radix-5 (i.e., base-5) notation?
questions.subject: Digital Logic

questions.text:
Consider 4-variable functions f1, f2, f3, f4 expressed in sum-of-minterms form as given below.

\(f1 = \sum(0,2,3,5,7,8,11,13)\)
\(f2 = \sum(1,3,5,7,11,13,15)\)
\(f3 = \sum(0,1,4,11)\)
\(f4 = \sum(0,2,6,13)\)

With respect to the circuit given above, which of the following options is/are CORRECT?
questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.solution:
In the circuit, f1 and f2 feed an AND gate, f3 and f4 feed an OR gate, and the two outputs feed an XOR gate giving Y.
f1 AND f2: common minterms \(\{3,5,7,11,13\}\).
f3 OR f4: union \(\{0,1,2,4,6,11,13\}\).
XOR keeps minterms in exactly one set: \(\{3,5,7\} \cup \{0,1,2,4,6\} = \{0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}\).
So \(Y = \sum(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7) = \Pi(8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15)\): C and D correct.
A and B describe the same function \(\sum(0,1,2,11,13)\), which is wrong.

questions.text: Let \(G\) be an undirected connected graph in which every edge has a positive integer weight. Suppose that every spanning tree in \(G\) has even weight. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE for every such graph \(G\) ?

options.label: A
options.text: All edges in \(G\) have even weight

options.label: B
options.text: All edges in \(G\) have even weight OR all edges in \(G\) have odd weight

options.label: C
options.text: In each cycle \(C\) in \(G\), all edges in \(C\) have even weight

options.label: D
options.text: In each cycle \(C\) in \(G\), either all edges in \(C\) have even weight OR all edges in \(C\) have odd weight

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
Key fact: if \(e\) and \(f\) lie on a common cycle \(C\), take a spanning tree \(T\) containing every edge of \(C\) except \(e\). Then \(T - f + e\) is also a spanning tree, and both have even weight, so \(w(e) \equiv w(f) \pmod 2\). Hence all edges of a cycle have the same parity: D is true.
A and C: false. A triangle with weights 1, 1, 1 has every spanning tree of weight 2.
B: false. Take that odd triangle and attach a pendant edge of weight 2: every spanning tree weighs \(1 + 1 + 2 = 4\), yet the graph has both odd and even edges.

questions.text:
Consider a context-free grammar \(G\) with the following 3 rules.

\(S \rightarrow aS,\ S \rightarrow aSbS,\ S \rightarrow c\)

Let \(w \in L(G)\). Let \(n_a(w), n_b(w), n_c(w)\) denote the number of times \(a, b, c\) occur in \(w\), respectively. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.solution:
Let a derivation use \(S \rightarrow aS\) \(p\) times, \(S \rightarrow aSbS\) \(q\) times and \(S \rightarrow c\) \(r\) times. Then \(n_a = p + q\), \(n_b = q\), \(n_c = r\). Each \(aSbS\) adds one extra S and each c removes one, starting from one S, so \(r = q + 1\).
A: false. \(n_a = n_b\) when \(p = 0\), for example acbc.
B: true. \(n_c - 2 = q - 1 < q \leq n_a\).
C: true. \(n_c = q + 1 = n_b + 1\).
D: false. For w = c, \(n_c = 1\) but \(2n_b = 0\).

questions.text:
Consider a disk with the following specifications: rotation speed of 6000 RPM, average seek time of 5 milliseconds, 500 sectors/track, 512-byte sectors.

A file has content stored in 3000 sectors located randomly on the disk. Assuming average rotational latency, the total time (in seconds, rounded off to 2 decimal places) to read the entire file from the disk is _________
questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.solution:
One rotation: \(60/6000\) s \(= 10\) ms, so the average rotational latency is 5 ms.
Transfer time of one sector: \(10/500 = 0.02\) ms.
The sectors are random, so each needs its own seek and latency: \(5 + 5 + 0.02 = 10.02\) ms per sector.
Total: \(3000 \times 10.02 = 30060\) ms \(= 30.06\) s.

questions.text: Consider a TCP connection operating at a point of time with the congestion window of size 12 MSS (Maximum Segment Size), when a timeout occurs due to packet loss. Assuming that all the segments transmitted in the next two RTTs (Round Trip Time) are acknowledged correctly, the congestion window size (in MSS) during the third RTT will be _________
questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.solution:
On a timeout, the threshold becomes \(12/2 = 6\) MSS and the window drops to 1 MSS (slow start).
First RTT after the timeout: window 1. All acknowledged, so it doubles: second RTT window 2. Doubling again: third RTT window 4, still below the threshold of 6.

questions.text: Consider an Ethernet segment with a transmission speed of \(10^8\) bits/sec and a maximum segment length of 500 meters. If the speed of propagation of the signal in the medium is \(2 \times 10^8\) meters/sec, then the minimum frame size (in bits) required for collision detection is _________
questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.solution:
Propagation delay: \(T_p = \frac{500}{2 \times 10^8} = 2.5\ \mu s\).
For collision detection the transmission time must be at least the round trip, \(2T_p = 5\ \mu s\).
Minimum frame size \(= 10^8 \times 5 \times 10^{-6} = 500\) bits.

questions.text:
A functional dependency \(F: X \rightarrow Y\) is termed as a useful functional dependency if and only if it satisfies all the following three conditions:

- \(X\) is not the empty set.
- \(Y\) is not the empty set.
- Intersection of \(X\) and \(Y\) is the empty set.

For a relation \(R\) with 4 attributes, the total number of possible useful functional dependencies is ________
questions.subject: Databases
questions.solution:
Each of the 4 attributes goes to \(X\), to \(Y\) or to neither (they cannot be in both): \(3^4 = 81\) ways.
Remove those with \(X\) empty (\(2^4 = 16\)) and those with \(Y\) empty (16), adding back the one with both empty: \(81 - 16 - 16 + 1 = 50\).

questions.text: A processor with 16 general purpose registers uses a 32-bit instruction format. The instruction format consists of an opcode field, an addressing mode field, two register operand fields, and a 16-bit scalar field. If 8 addressing modes are to be supported, the maximum number of unique opcodes possible for every addressing mode is _________
questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.solution:
Register field: \(\log_2 16 = 4\) bits, two of them: 8 bits. Addressing mode: \(\log_2 8 = 3\) bits. Scalar: 16 bits.
Opcode bits \(= 32 - 16 - 8 - 3 = 5\), so \(2^5 = 32\) opcodes.

questions.text: A non-pipelined instruction execution unit operating at 2 GHz takes an average of 6 cycles to execute an instruction of a program P. The unit is then redesigned to operate on a 5-stage pipeline at 2 GHz. Assume that the ideal throughput of the pipelined unit is 1 instruction per cycle. In the execution of program P, 20% instructions incur an average of 2 cycles stall due to data hazards and 20% instructions incur an average of 3 cycles stall due to control hazards. The speedup (rounded off to one decimal place) obtained by the pipelined design over the non-pipelined design is _________
questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.solution:
Pipelined CPI \(= 1 + 0.2 \times 2 + 0.2 \times 3 = 2\).
Both run at 2 GHz, so speedup \(= \frac{6}{2} = 3.0\).

questions.text: The number of distinct minimum-weight spanning trees of the following graph is _________
questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.chapter: Graph Traversals, Spanning Trees and Shortest Paths
questions.solution:
Edges: weight 1: a-b, a-f, c-d, d-e. Weight 2: a-g, b-g, f-g, c-g, d-g, e-g. Weight 3: b-c, f-e.
The four weight-1 edges form no cycle, so every MST contains them. They leave three components: \(\{a, b, f\}\), \(\{c, d, e\}\) and \(\{g\}\).
Two more edges are needed, and weight-2 edges suffice: one from g to \(\{a, b, f\}\) (3 choices: a-g, b-g, f-g) and one from g to \(\{c, d, e\}\) (3 choices: c-g, d-g, e-g). The weight-3 edges are never needed.
Number of MSTs \(= 3 \times 3 = 9\), each of weight 8.

questions.text: The chromatic number of a graph is the minimum number of colours used in a *proper* colouring of the graph. The chromatic number of the following graph is _________
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
Number the 8 vertices 0 to 7 around the octagon. The edges are the octagon sides \(i, i+1\), plus the horizontal, vertical and slanted chords, each of which joins \(i\) to \(i + 3\) (mod 8).
Every edge joins vertices whose numbers differ by an odd amount (1 or 3), so it always joins an even vertex to an odd vertex: the graph is bipartite. In fact each even vertex is joined to all four odd vertices, so it is \(K_{4,4}\).
Colour the even vertices one colour and the odd vertices another. It has edges, so it needs at least 2 colours. Chromatic number 2.

questions.text:
A processor uses a 32-bit instruction format and supports byte-addressable memory access. The ISA of the processor has 150 distinct instructions. The instructions are equally divided into two types, namely R-type and I-type, whose formats are shown below.

R-type Instruction Format:

| OPCODE | UNUSED | DST Register | SRC Register1 | SRC Register 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|

I-type Instruction Format:

| OPCODE | DST Register | SRC Register | # Immediate value/address |
|---|---|---|---|

In the OPCODE, 1 bit is used to distinguish between I-type and R-type instructions and the remaining bits indicate the operation. The processor has 50 architectural registers, and all register fields in the instructions are of equal size.

Let \(X\) be the number of bits used to encode the UNUSED field, \(Y\) be the number of bits used to encode the OPCODE field, and \(Z\) be the number of bits used to encode the immediate value/address field. The value of \(X + 2Y + Z\) is ________
questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.solution:
Each type has \(150/2 = 75\) operations, needing \(\lceil \log_2 75 \rceil = 7\) bits; with the type bit, \(Y = 8\).
Register fields: \(\lceil \log_2 50 \rceil = 6\) bits each.
R-type: \(8 + X + 3 \times 6 = 32\), so \(X = 6\).
I-type: \(8 + 6 + 6 + Z = 32\), so \(Z = 12\).
\(X + 2Y + Z = 6 + 16 + 12 = 34\).

questions.text: Let \(L_1\) be the language represented by the regular expression \(b^*ab^*(ab^*ab^*)^*\) and \(L_2 = \{w \in (a + b)^* \mid |w| \leq 4\}\), where \(|w|\) denotes the length of string \(w\). The number of strings in \(L_2\) which are also in \(L_1\) is ___________
questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.solution:
\(b^*ab^*\) gives one a, and each \(ab^*ab^*\) adds two more, with b's anywhere: \(L_1\) is the set of strings with an odd number of a's.
Of the \(2^n\) strings of length \(n \geq 1\), exactly half, \(2^{n-1}\), have an odd number of a's; the empty string has none.
Count for lengths 1 to 4: \(1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15\).

questions.text: Let \(Z_n\) be the group of integers \(\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, n-1\}\) with addition modulo \(n\) as the group operation. The number of elements in the group \(Z_2 \times Z_3 \times Z_4\) that are their own inverses is ________
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
An element is its own inverse when adding it to itself gives the identity, componentwise.
In \(Z_2\): \(2x \equiv 0\) for \(x = 0, 1\): 2 choices. In \(Z_3\): only \(x = 0\): 1 choice. In \(Z_4\): \(x = 0, 2\): 2 choices.
Total \(= 2 \times 1 \times 2 = 4\).

questions.text:
Consider a 32-bit system with 4 KB page size and page table entries of size 4 bytes each. Assume 1 KB = \(2^{10}\) bytes. The OS uses a 2-level page table for memory management, with the page table containing an outer page directory and an inner page table. The OS allocates a page for the outer page directory upon process creation. The OS uses demand paging when allocating memory for the inner page table, i.e., a page of the inner page table is allocated only if it contains at least one valid page table entry.

An active process in this system accesses 2000 unique pages during its execution, and none of the pages are swapped out to disk. After it completes the page accesses, let X denote the minimum and Y denote the maximum number of pages across the two levels of the page table of the process.

The value of X+Y is ________
questions.subject: Operating System
questions.solution:
Page number: \(32 - 12 = 20\) bits. A page holds \(4096/4 = 1024\) entries, so the outer directory has \(2^{10} = 1024\) entries (one page) and each inner page table maps 1024 pages.
Minimum: the 2000 pages packed together need \(\lceil 2000/1024 \rceil = 2\) inner pages, so \(X = 1 + 2 = 3\).
Maximum: each page in a different inner table, but there are only 1024 inner tables, so at most 1024 inner pages: \(Y = 1 + 1024 = 1025\).
\(X + Y = 3 + 1025 = 1028\).

questions.text:
Consider the following augmented grammar, which is to be parsed with a SLR parser. The set of terminals is \(\{a,b,c,d,\#,@\}\)

\(S' \rightarrow S\)
\(S \rightarrow SS \mid Aa \mid bAc \mid Bc \mid bBa\)
\(A \rightarrow d\#\)
\(B \rightarrow @\)

Let \(I_0 = CLOSURE(\{S' \rightarrow \bullet S\})\). The number of items in the set \(GOTO(I_0, S)\) is ___________
questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.solution:
\(I_0\) contains \(S' \rightarrow \bullet S\), \(S \rightarrow \bullet SS\) and the other S items, \(A \rightarrow \bullet d\#\), \(B \rightarrow \bullet @\).
Moving the dot over S: \(S' \rightarrow S\bullet\) and \(S \rightarrow S\bullet S\).
The closure of \(S \rightarrow S\bullet S\) adds all five S items \(S \rightarrow \bullet SS\), \(S \rightarrow \bullet Aa\), \(S \rightarrow \bullet bAc\), \(S \rightarrow \bullet Bc\), \(S \rightarrow \bullet bBa\), and then, because of \(\bullet A\) and \(\bullet B\), \(A \rightarrow \bullet d\#\) and \(B \rightarrow \bullet @\).
Total \(= 2 + 5 + 2 = 9\) items.
